bug_semantics: On an installation whose active cluster credential was the compiled-in default, any network client that copied the public source constant into X-WolfStack-Secret passed require_auth() as the synthetic cluster-node principal without a session, API key, or user account. That principal could call management endpoints, including POST /api/containers/{runtime}/{id}/exec, which passed attacker-controlled command text to sh -c inside the selected Docker or LXC container as root.
flaw_origin: Commit 2d2d371527bde1e9d72eadcd2ee3e7c0ee3adfbc replaced the parent implementation's per-node, randomly generated /etc/wolfstack/cluster.key with one source-published CLUSTER_SECRET shared by every installation and made load_cluster_secret() return that constant. The pre-existing request gate compared X-WolfStack-Secret with state.cluster_secret without any source-address or recorded-peer check, so this replacement converted possession of public source text into authentication.
ai_marker: absent — the raw BIC commit object names human author and committer Paul C <paulc@wolf.uk.com> and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI attribution, or other trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/wolfsoftwaresystemsltd/WolfStack/security/advisories/GHSA-r3mw-2wmq-j6jg states affected versions <=25.9.1, patched version 25.9.2, the any-source X-WolfStack-Secret bypass, the cluster-node identity, and the container exec impact. It limits affected configurations to nodes still using/falling back to the built-in default; nodes already rotated to a per-install secret were not affected.

git log -L 25,32:src/auth/mod.rs v25.9.1 and git log -S of the exact constant identify 2d2d371527bde1e9d72eadcd2ee3e7c0ee3adfbc as the first commit that writes CLUSTER_SECRET. Its focused diff replaces CLUSTER_KEY_PATH plus random UUID generation/persistence with the fixed source constant and CLUSTER_SECRET.to_string(); Cargo.toml changes 5.9.3 to 5.9.4 in the same implementation commit. An all-ref -S search found no earlier copy of the constant.

Direct parent-tree verification: git grep of the exact constant at a05c0870a84981d639067719de6be2395c958852 exits 1 with no match. parent:src/auth/mod.rs instead reads /etc/wolfstack/cluster.key, generates two random UUID-derived values when absent, persists the result, and chmods it 0600. Thus the public shared credential mechanism is absent in the immediate parent.

At the BIC tree, src/api/mod.rs require_auth() reads X-WolfStack-Secret, compares it against state.cluster_secret, and returns cluster-node on equality, with no peer/source check. At v25.9.1, src/api/mod.rs:7144-7153 shows POST /api/containers/{runtime}/{id}/exec guarded only by require_auth() before invoking sh -c with the supplied command.

Lifecycle history explains but does not replace the BIC: c8e3c7f08ba3c4a172e311ecd83b0419ebd4a6c1 temporarily removed the constant for a per-install secret in 11.26.3; 15772636355c6159d6c2dd6a608265ac65f4c208 restored it in 11.26.4 to repair inter-node communication. Because 15772636355c6159d6c2dd6a608265ac65f4c208 is a revert/reintroduction of lines first authored by 2d2d371527bde1e9d72eadcd2ee3e7c0ee3adfbc, it is not the smallest original BIC. Later custom-secret rotation retained the built-in value as a fallback, leaving unrotated/read-failure configurations exposed.

Direct fix 3767540356e16130717abe4d7846bd5a20eae71b introduces validate_inter_node_secret_from(provided, in_memory, peer), recognizes the published default before checking in-memory/on-disk slots, and accepts it only from transport-level peer_addr() values recorded in nodes.json; missing or unrecorded peers fail closed. This closes both the explicit default branch and the subtle case where the in-memory/on-disk slot itself contains the default.

The direct fix lands on master in merge 29aad2c2a6b5dd45d9138b9d605e6314d4d4b4ac. git merge-base --is-ancestor shows 3767540356e16130717abe4d7846bd5a20eae71b is not an ancestor of v25.9.1 (exit 1) but is an ancestor of v25.9.2 (exit 0). The boundary tags resolve to v25.9.1=9de91b706a26ac6067cb33a188966d485c67d9ad and v25.9.2=3303cb7248917524459fab22a29c6877ddaca68b; the latter contains the fix merge (and, due the repository's tag placement, the immediately following 25.9.3 hardening merge as well).

git cat-file commit 2d2d371527bde1e9d72eadcd2ee3e7c0ee3adfbc shows one parent, human author/committer Paul C <paulc@wolf.uk.com>, and a plain explanatory message with no trailers. The BIC is a direct, atomic source change rather than a merge, move, backport, or reconstructable squash aggregate, so no decomposition member supersedes it.
reasoning: The safe immediate parent already had the relevant inter-node authentication gate, but its expected value was generated uniquely per node and stored locally. The BIC's security-relevant delta is therefore minimal and causal: it replaces that secret source with a credential identical across installations and visible in the public repository, while leaving the equality-based X-WolfStack-Secret gate to confer cluster-node authority. That is the first point at which public knowledge alone authenticates a remote caller. Line history records a later removal and revert, but the protocol excludes a revert as the origin when the original vulnerable authorship is available. The affected boundary is coherent: the BIC labels the source 5.9.4; the vulnerable mechanism remains reachable in v25.9.1, while the direct 25.9.2 fix is absent from v25.9.1 and present in v25.9.2. The fix routes every presentation of the default through recorded-peer validation before ordinary secret comparisons, eliminating the bypass for an arbitrary remote source. Finally, AI attribution is evaluated only from the BIC commit object; its human identities and lack of AI/bot/trailer markers require NOT_AI regardless of any signals that might exist on later lifecycle commits.
